messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Sev2 — Multiple KV-cache shard hot paths showing imbalance and NCCL stall signals on tp-shard-group-7. Auto-scaler churn observed, cache memory spike -> OOM evictions. Affected: 3 high-traffic customers. Paging oncall.

mike_oncall: ack. I'm on it, taking pager. tagging @julia_sre and @kevin_runtime. give me a minute to pull logs. :eyes:

julia_sre: joining. grabbing metrics + dmesg from nodes in tp-shard-group-7. seeing repeated `NCCL WARN` entries and a flurry of `kv_cache: shard_unavailable` traces.

kevin_runtime: noticed a recent tweak to continuous-batching config rolled ~45m ago in that pool (batch_window_ms=20 -> 8) — could be spike interacting with shard assignment.

aditya_ml: also got an alert from model-quality: continuous-batch hit perf cliff for long-context loads, causing huge KV cache growth for some prefixes.

mike_oncall: initial impact: user-visible tail latency spikes and ~10% 5xx for long-context endpoints routed to that shard group. small % of requests hit fallback and slowed down. marking incident.p1=false incident.p2=true.

julia_sre: attaching short logs: ```
[2026-03-15T03:12:10Z] NCCL WARN: AllReduce timeout after 120000ms, rank 2 stuck
[2026-03-15T03:12:11Z] runtime: kv_cache shard 5: eviction flood, mem_use=94%
[2026-03-15T03:12:12Z] runtime: shard_assignment: computed uneven_partitioning -> weights: [0.02,0.45,0.01,0.47,0.05]
```

kevin_runtime: that's the bug pattern — the shard hashing function returns skewed weights when batch sizes drop and many requests have identical prefix keys; combined with TP partitioning it leaves some GPUs idle and others overloaded, then NCCL waits for stragglers.

aditya_ml: workaround idea: force deterministic even partitioning for tp-shards and temporarily disable prefix coalescing in continuous-batching. reduces throughput but stabilizes latency.

mike_oncall: propose mitigation plan: 1) Disable continuous-batching on tp-shard-group-7 via config flag 2) Roll runtime hotfix to enforce even KV shard assignment fallback 3) Restart runtime pods in that pool 4) Monitor customer impact and escalate if needed. anyone object?

julia_sre: +1. please set maintenance flag and adjust autoscaler buffer to avoid further churn.

kevin_runtime: I can push a hotfix to the shard assignment routine (simple fallback that uses `node_index % num_shards` when imbalance detected). small patch, build now.

mike_oncall: tara_support, can you open tickets and notify the three customers? we should give ETA ~20-30m for mitigation and note degraded latency.

tara_support: on it. sending notices now and posting short update on status page: "Investigating intermittent latency for long-context generation; mitigation in progress."

kevin_runtime: hotfix branch ready. test-run in staging succeeded. patch: ```diff
- weights = compute_dynamic_weights(prefix_keys)
+ weights = compute_dynamic_weights(prefix_keys)
+ if detect_imbalance(weights):
+     weights = even_partition(num_shards)  # fallback
```
building image rwd-runtime:hotfix-kv-shard-20260315

deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy rwd-runtime:hotfix-kv-shard-20260315 -> canary pool tp-shard-group-7-canary

deploy-bot: Canary deploy successful (3/3 health).

mike_oncall: good. rolling to remaining nodes in tp-shard-group-7 with graceful restart. also toggling continuous-batching off for that pool: `rwdctl config set --pool tp-shard-group-7 continuous_batching=false`

julia_sre: issuing rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart ds/rwd-runtime --selector=tp-group=7 -n prod`

incident-bot: NOTE: maintenance mode enabled for tp-shard-group-7 by mike_oncall.

kevin_runtime: watching logs. initial nodes coming back clean, NCCL WARN frequency dropping. KV cache mem_use trending down.

aditya_ml: model-level perf back to baseline on test traffic once shard fallback applied.

mike_oncall: customer impact update: error rate down to ~1.2% from 10%, tail latency improving. continue to monitor for next 30m before lifting mitigation.

tara_support: customers A and C acknowledged the update, B asked for postmortem — created CS ticket CS-4821 and linked incident thread.

julia_sre: collecting artifacts for postmortem: kernel logs, NCCL traces, runtime shard metrics, recent config changes. assigning retention to 14 days.

kevin_runtime: will open PR for the shard assignment fallback and add a config gate so we can re-enable continuous-batching once we have a fix that avoids key-coalescing pathologies. PR: https://git.internal/rwd/runtime/pull/409

deploy-bot: Hotfix rolled to 100% for tp-shard-group-7. No regressions reported in canary window.

mike_oncall: time check: mitigation completed ~25m after page. handing off to @aditya_ml to own post-incident analysis and follow-up actions (quantify perf cliff and root cause). I'll remain available for follow-ups.

aditya_ml: taking postmortem. next actions: 1) schedule evals for continuous-batching changes with long-context prompts 2) quantify unit-economics cost of fallback 3) propose automated detect-and-fallback to even partitioning in runtime.

mike_oncall: thanks all. closing pager for now, will mark incident as mitigated. please add any remaining notes here. :white_check_mark:
